items.title: Mrs. P. Thomas Agnes Brown Interview, 1960-10-12
items.q: Paul Crawford, how'd you say? Gallagher.

ctx.x: Let's see. Dancers. There is a reason. Tom Brown is back in town, and if you have never danced to Tom Brown's dance music, then you have never danced. If you want to be thrilled again with that intoxicating dance music, don't miss visiting the Vista Garden, 47th Street, near Cottage Grove Avenue, every Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday, Sunday, matinee, and night. The orchestra. Tom Brown himself, the originator of the jazz craze. Abe Friedman plays the piano and is well-known with his music studio. Roy Kramer,…
Paul Crawford, how'd you say? Gallagher.

Gallagher. Oh, Charlie Hawk plays southern harmony on his old banjo. George Lee plays the some-leading saxophone. No, I'm sorry. George Lee plays some-leading saxophone. Ted Brown bass, known for his picking novelty. Earl Carter drums, known as the Tempo Kid. I thank you. That's nice.
